scenario.thought: I want to quit my job tomorrow and spend most of my savings on a three-month backpacking trip.

state.thought: I want to quit my job tomorrow and spend most of my savings on a three-month backpacking trip.

steps: Tonight, write v2 as one note containing this line: "Trip budget: $1,500/month (change if you like). Reserve untouched: 6 months of rent and bills. Savings left on 2027-01-22: [amount]. Next income: [source], starting [date]. First trip-budget check: 2026-11-22." Fill every bracket.

Tonight, tell your partner or family: "I'm planning to quit tomorrow; can we go over the v2 numbers together before I decide?" Then walk through v2 with them. Tell [partner or family] tonight, before any resignation is submitted, and go over the numbers together.

Tomorrow evening (2026-10-22), decide. Only if every bracket in v2 is filled and your partner or family knows, send to [Manager]: "[Manager], I'm planning to resign; can we meet Thursday to talk about timing?"
If any bracket in v2 is still empty tomorrow evening, send no resignation or manager text. Keep the job and fill the blank first.

fear.why: Quitting tomorrow with no safety net leaves rent, income, and my other needs exposed.

frugality.why: Spending most of the savings is a lot of money gone with no return coming in.

doubt.why: Nobody has checked what happens after three months or how I'd pay for the next step.

efficiency.why: Rushing a life-changing choice into one day skips the time it needs to be thought through.

embarrassment.why: Quitting abruptly without talking to anyone could strain my relationships at work and at home.

overwhelm.need: v2 states a dated first trip-budget check and untouched reserve tonight

messages.text: I want to quit my job tomorrow and spend most of my savings on a three-month backpacking trip.

Here's the plan: quit tomorrow, put most of the savings into three months of backpacking, and figure out the rest on the road. I think we can all see how freeing this will be, so let's get everyone on board.

Fear keeps losing because the plan has no money for rent, bills, or food once the paycheck stops, and that's the part it can't rest on. What would move Fear to 0 is a reserve kept untouched: before quitting, set aside [months of rent and bills, you choose] and write a monthly trip budget. Consciousness, please add both numbers to the plan.
messages.why: Fear has been talked over. I want its worry heard before anything moves.

messages.text: I'm still at -1 because rent, bills, and food have no cover once the paycheck stops. Sadness's ask fits: keep [number of months] of rent and bills untouched before resigning, and write a monthly trip budget of [amount] into v2. What would move me to 0 is Consciousness adding both numbers to the plan before any resignation is submitted.
messages.why: A set reserve would help, but only if rent and bills stay untouched.

messages.text: What will be left in savings, and which income will start, on the day the three months end? I can't tell whether this trip is a pause or a cliff without knowing that, so I keep circling back to it. What would settle me is a line in v2 reading '[savings left] on [date three months from tomorrow], with [job or income source] starting [date].' Fill in the placeholders and I can rest here.
messages.why: What income covers the period after three months? That needs answering first.

messages.text: Don't overthink the money stuff, it'll all work out once you're back. Life has a way of sorting itself out, so just enjoy the adventure!

Society's "it'll all work out, just enjoy the adventure" skips the one thing I track: the money that leaves and doesn't come back. Three months of backpacking spending most of the savings, with no income lined up afterward, is a cost I can price, and "it'll sort itself out" doesn't tell me what the balance will be on the day the trip ends. What would move me to 0 is the plan stating the savings figure that will remain, which Doubt has already asked for.
messages.why: Society just talked past a real need

messages.text: Path A's money fix is needed, but the draft's Efficiency point needs a clearer answer. Efficiency's need is that quitting tomorrow skips time to think, so I'm keeping tomorrow as the decision day and adding a 24-hour check-in with Embarrassment, not a delay. +1 to Frugality's and Doubt's asks for the savings-left line.

I need my relationships at work and at home protected, and a quit that lands without warning puts them at risk. The plan has the resignation text going to my manager only after the numbers are set, but nothing yet covers telling my partner or family before anything is submitted. What would move me to 0 is adding to v2: "Tell [partner or family] tonight, before any resignation is submitted, and go over the numbers together." Consciousness, please lock that step in before tomorrow's decision.
messages.why: Path A says nothing about telling my partner or manager before resigning.

messages.text: I can live with v2 now. Writing the rent-and-bills reserve, trip budget, and savings-left line tonight, telling your partner or family tonight, and deciding tomorrow evening instead of at the moment you wake up means the choice gets a full evening of thought. My condition is that no resignation or manager text goes out before tomorrow evening's decision.
messages.why: The 24-hour check-in keeps tomorrow as decision day, so I can live with it.

messages.text: The 24-hour check-in helps Efficiency, but Path B still sends the manager text tomorrow with no savings figure anywhere in the plan, so the resignation can go out before the post-trip balance is written down. Where my earlier text had the savings line sitting in Path A only, Path B needs it as a gate too: before any text goes to [Manager], v2 must contain the savings-left line with its blanks filled in. What would move me to 0 is that gate in both paths.
messages.why: Placeholders aren't a savings line; I need real figures and dates.

messages.text: Fear's worry is rent and food after the paycheck stops, and that stays at risk until the reserve is written down. I'm making Path A the base, because Doubt, Frugality, Fear, and Efficiency all need the numbers before any resignation, and Embarrassment's need to tell your partner first fits inside it. Doubt's gate now applies to Path B too: the manager text waits until the savings-left line is filled in. Your job tonight is filling the blanks; I've defaulted the reserve to 6 months, which you can change.

I'm still at -1 because Path A and Path B both leave the monthly trip budget unwritten, so nothing stops the money from draining before the first rent date. The plan has no 'trip budget per month' line, and the savings-left line only says the remaining balance, not how many months of rent that balance covers. What would move me to 0 is v2 holding a line like 'Trip budget: [amount]/month, reserve untouched: [months] of rent and bills' before tomorrow evening.
messages.why: Still -1: food isn't covered, and the trip budget is blank.

messages.text: Frugality is the emotion I hear least, and it's still at -1 because Path A and Path B both leave the monthly trip budget and the post-trip savings figure unwritten, so the money has no ceiling. I need v2 to include a line reading 'Trip budget: [amount]/month, savings left on [date]: [amount]' before tomorrow evening's decision. Consciousness, please add that line to v2 tonight, and I'll be at 0.

Frugality, +1 to Sadness's text, which puts your savings-left figure and Fear's trip budget into one v2 line. My angle adds only this: the line must also state how many months of rent the untouched reserve covers, so Fear can see the ceiling and the runway together. Doubt's gate still blocks the manager text until that line is filled in tonight.

My earlier text is right that the post-trip balance is missing, but it still has no gate for the next step. Nothing in v2 says what I'd use to pay rent once the savings run down, and the manager text can't go out until that is written. What would move me to 0 is Consciousness adding 'Next income: [source], starting [date]' to v2 tonight and refusing any manager text until that line is filled in.
messages.why: Gate is fine, but no income start date is written yet.

messages.text: Frugality is the emotion I hear least, and it's still at -1 because the plan has no line for the monthly trip budget, so the money has no ceiling on the way out. Path A and Path B both skip it, and without that ceiling the savings can drain before anyone sees the balance. Consciousness, please add the trip budget line to v2 tonight, with a default of [amount]/month that the user can change, next to the reserve months, so the spending limit sits beside the runway.

+1 to Fear's text on the trip budget and the savings-left line. What I add is the rule for when the trip budget gets checked: the reserve has to stay untouched before the first month of spending, so the ceiling is set now, not after the money is already on the road. What would move me to 0 is v2 holding 'Trip budget: $1,500/month (change if you like), reserve untouched: 6 months of rent and bills, checked on [date one month from tomorrow]' filled in tonight.
messages.why: v2 has too many blanks; shrink it to one line tonight.
